receiptDeadlineMinutes.provenance: Kalshi Weather Index Methodology (certified, MIAWINDEX.pdf and its siblings): S + D, D = 300 seconds. Measured 2026-10-18: 148 polled minutes had no published value before 277 s and all had one by 358 s

marketSpanMinutes.provenance: open_time to close_time of all 15,770 settled hourly index markets, 2026-10-01..10-17 (services/forecasting-service/data/records/2026-10-16-hourly-index-station-lattice, data/events)

confidence.provenance: one-sided 95%: Clopper and Pearson 1934; Efron and Tibshirani 1993 section 13. Results are reported at 0.01 and 0.10 beside it

resamples.provenance: block bootstrap replicates; the percentile interval of a tail quantile is stable to a few percent at 200 (Efron and Tibshirani 1993 section 13.3)

tailRoot.provenance: the number of tail exceedances k = n^0.5 (the square-root rule; Hall 1990; Drees and Kaufmann 1998 choose k from the data and land near it for light tails)

tailFloor.provenance: fewest exceedances a generalized Pareto fit is attempted on (Hosking and Wallis 1987)

tailIndexBound.provenance: the shape is kept in [-0.5, 0.5], where probability-weighted moments are regular and the tail has a finite mean (Hosking and Wallis 1987)

regimeCandidates.provenance: counts of volatility regimes tried; the one with the lowest hold-out pinball loss is used

regimeQuantiles.provenance: move quantiles the regime count is scored on (the part of the distribution a decision uses)

holdOutFraction.provenance: the latest quarter of the training window scores the regime count

minimumAnchors.provenance: fewest anchors a stratum is fitted on

tailKeepFactor.provenance: the bootstrap keeps the largest 4 k moves of a stratum: a refit uses k, and the threshold moves with the resample

autocorrelationWindow.provenance: Sokal (1997) automatic windowing: the window is the smallest M with M >= 5 tau(M)

tablePrecisionExponent.provenance: the table runs to 2^-20, about 1e-6: below the order of one wrong decision per year (4 cities x 24 hours x 365 days = 35,040 decisions, 2^-15) with a factor of 32 beyond
